newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-SMILING KIKPETER KEEPS DATE WITH DESTINY.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-SMILING KIKPETER KEEPS DATE WITH DESTINY.

text.p: Wilson Kipketer kept his date with destiny on Friday when he sprinted home to retain the world 800 metres title.
"Yes, I was pretty certain I was going to get the gold I must be honest," said the Kenyan-born Dane with the disarming smile.
"I didn't take the victory for granted because there were four rounds of competition and anything can happen. But I had my game plan, my secrets, and it all worked tonight."
The only surprise was that Kipketer's victory was not quite as emphatic as many had predicted and that the field were still within 20 metres of him at the finish.
"That was just the way it turned out," he said. "You can't plan every race exactly, but I did what I thought I had to do to win this race and it worked."
Kipketer, always favourite to win here, equalled Seb Coe's 16-year-old world record of 1:41.73 in Stockholm on July 7.
His winning time on Thursday of 1:43.38 never threatened the joint record but Kipketer said afterwards it was never his intention to try and break the record here.

"I am fed up talking about the world record," he said, "I wanted to win the gold medal and the title. People who understand the sport know why that would be my priority, the world record does not interest me at the moment."
Kipketer blasted through the first 200 in a speedy 23.47 seconds, clocked 49.68 for the first lap and 53.70 for the second.

While he was running his own race from the front, there was another race going on for the silver and bronze medals which ended with Cuban Norberto Tellez taking the silver in 1:44.00 and American Rich Kenah running a lifetime best of 1:44.25 to take the bronze.
Kipketer was unable to take part in the Olympics a year ago because the federation of Kenya, his birthplace, would not allow him to run for Denmark, his adopted homeland. In his absence
Verbjoern Rodal of Norway won the Olympic title but he was never in contention on Friday and finished fifth.
